subject: Echomark: request for billing accommodation after weekend latency spike
messages:
From: Dana Reed <dana@echomark.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & timeouts over weekend — Echomark impacted

Jonas,

Thanks for having us on standby. Quick note from our ops team: between Sat 2026-11-14 01:00 UTC and Sat 2026-11-14 07:05 UTC we saw sustained tail latencies on the /embed and /chat endpoints and several 500s for background ingestion jobs. Our SREs pulled metrics and are seeing the tenant-level SLO drop to ~97.2% for that 6 hour window (our agreement calls for 99.9%).

Impact: several customer-facing requests retried, search staleness for some sessions, and backlog on our nightly batch — customer support has logged ~120 tickets tied to delayed responses.

We appreciate Redwood's transparency on incidents historically; given the scale of the disruption, Echomark is requesting a billing accommodation: either one month of service credit for the legacy tenant (our oldest instance still on your shared pool) or a line-item credit offsetting the impacted usage (estimated at ~$9.5k for the month).

I've attached the compressed incident logs we collected and an initial timeline (echomark-incident-log.zip). Please advise next steps and a target for a formal remediation credit proposal so we can close this on our side.

Regards,
Dana Reed
Head of Infrastructure, Echomark
Dana Reed | Echomark
attachments: echomark-incident-log.zip

Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & timeouts over weekend — Echomark impacted

Dana —

Thanks for the clear notes and the logs. I'm really sorry Echomark experienced that regression over the weekend — I know how disruptive this is for your flows. I've looped Marissa (my manager) and Karthik (VP) since this is both an SLA impact and a contractual concession ask.

Immediate plan:
- I'll get Ops to validate the timeline and confirm root cause; internal ticket OPS-1824 has been created.
- For commercial accommodation, I'm proposing we start with a one-time offset equal to 20% of the November invoice as a placeholder while we finalize the quantified impact. Alternatively, if Echomark prefers a one-month service credit for the legacy tenant, we can consider that.

Can you confirm which you prefer (percentage credit vs. single-month credit)? Also, if you can flag the top three customer-facing endpoints impacted and send the CloudWatch traces for 11/14, that will help speed reconciliation.

I'll follow up once Marissa/Karthik advise on executive approval steps — aiming for a clear response by EOD Friday.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Why I recommend an accommodation: Echomark is mid-funnel expansion (product teams are evaluating Dedicated later this quarter). They've been a steady user for 18 months and the account lead expects a significant upsell if we preserve trust. A measured goodwill gesture now reduces churn risk.

Commercial proposal (my recommendation):
- Approve a one-time credit equivalent to 30% of the November invoice prorated to the impacted usage (estimated cost to Redwood: ~$12k).
- In addition, provide one complimentary two-week Premium Support window (zero charge) so Echomark can validate stability after the fixes.

Operational ask: billing will need a formal memo and journal entry if we proceed; I've attached a draft breakdown (proposed-credit-breakdown.xlsx) and the incident timeline PDF from Echomark.

If you can greenlight this (or suggest a lower threshold), I'll draft the customer message and route to Billing to apply the credit.

-Marissa
